aboutH2: Round Lake Treatment Centre: First Nations Culture-Based Addiction Treatment near Armstrong, BC
intro: Round Lake Treatment Centre provides a 42 or 39 day residential program for individuals who have not fully recovered from the physiological effects of drugs and alcohol. The program is focused on motivational experiential counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), psychodynamic therapy, and sensorimotor psychotherapies, which are conducted in a group setting. The program is suitable for individuals who do not require detox and are emotionally stable to engage in counseling. The goal is to empower clients to take personal responsibility and recognize their own worth and potential.

Round Lake Treatment Centre is internationally CARF accredited and practices under Trauma Informed Practices. The program is led by the Program Director’s mantra, “We are here to serve; it is all about the clients.” The daily rate for residential treatment is $200.00 CDN per day.

pillars.title: Safe and Supportive Environment
pillars.body: Round Lake Treatment Centre practices trauma-informed care, and a safe, supportive environment is key to success. The center is located in a serene environment surrounded by nature. Clients have access to the Recovery Lodge, which features amazing views, a gym, a library, and healthy meals. There are also opportunities for sightseeing and shopping in town. Transportation is provided for scheduled events and essential appointments. For status First Nations clients, treatment is covered by the First Nations Health Authority.

pillars.title: Culture Is Treatment
pillars.body: "Culture Is Treatment" is the centre's own philosophy, and the program is organised around the Medicine Wheel and the balance of physical, mental, spiritual and emotional health. Clients smudge every morning, and they are given sage and materials to make a smudge kit they can take home. Elders come in regularly to share traditional teachings, language and song, and to lead nature walks. Twice a year, clients usually help harvest plant medicines in the hills around Round Lake. The website currently lists sweat lodge and pipe ceremonies as postponed under COVID-19 protocols. Round Lake says the spiritual side of the program is meant to sit alongside each person's own beliefs, and it welcomes people of all cultures.

pillars.title: An Aftercare Plan, a Refresher and a Recovery Home
pillars.body: Before you go home you write an aftercare and relapse prevention plan with your counsellor, and the centre asks you to book a post-treatment appointment with your home counsellor before you even arrive. Past clients who have stayed sober can come back for a four-week refresher, joining a current group in its second week. If going straight home feels too risky, the Painted Turtle Lodge is a 10-bed recovery home on the same property. It opened in 2017, and residents can stay up to six months. Rent is $400 a month ($600 for a couple) with meals included, because grants pay most of the cost.

overviewH2: Round Lake Treatment Centre: Center Overview
overview: The Round Lake Treatment Centre is a specialized rehab facility located in an Indian reserve that offers comprehensive treatment programs for individuals struggling with addiction. With a capacity of 36 beds, the facility provides residential programs that last between five and six weeks, followed by three weeks of aftercare for patients. The focus of the treatment is based on aboriginal holistic healing methods, which includes different therapies such as 12 step programs, individual and group counseling, family therapy, art and nature therapy, yoga, and meditation. The center also has a team of wise elders and 12 step speakers who work in collaboration with the patients to help them overcome their addiction.

The facility provides a supportive, safe, and comfortable environment with a range of amenities, such as residential drug rehab programs and substance abuse treatment. The center employs evidence-based practices and holistic therapy approaches that help the patients restore physical, emotional, and mental balance. Nutritional counseling is also provided, which helps the patients build a healthy lifestyle. Overall, the Round Lake Treatment Centre is committed to providing its patients with personalized and effective treatment programs that meet their unique needs and help them achieve long-term recovery.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Round Lake Treatment Centre cost?
faqs.a: Self-pay treatment costs $200 a day, which covers room and board, counselling, nursing and a psychologist if needed. At that rate a 42-day stay comes to $8,400, and the full amount is due on admission. Status First Nations clients pay nothing, and people on income assistance may qualify for per diem funding through the provincial ministry or a user fee subsidy from the regional ADS office.

faqs.q: Is treatment covered for First Nations clients?
faqs.a: Yes. Treatment for status First Nations clients is covered by the First Nations Health Authority, with no subsidy application needed beyond the status number on the application. FNHA also pays up to $80 for the medical exam. Some bands fund treatment too, so it is worth asking your band social worker, and Métis and non-status clients on income assistance can apply for provincial per diem funding.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for Round Lake's treatment program?
faqs.a: Individuals who have not fully recovered from the physiological effects of drugs and alcohol and are emotionally stable to engage in counseling can apply.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral, and can people from outside BC attend?
faqs.a: You need a referral, because Round Lake does not accept self-referrals. An alcohol and drug, mental health or family counsellor applies for you after at least six one-hour sessions in the past three months, and agrees to see you again after treatment. Since October 2019 the centre has only taken BC residents who have lived in the province for at least three months and hold an active BC Services Card.

faqs.q: What is the duration of the program offered by Round Lake Treatment Center?
faqs.a: Round Lake Treatment Center provides a 42 or 39 day residential program.

No, Round Lake does not offer detox and has no medical withdrawal facilities. You need at least 14 full days free of alcohol and drugs before your intake date, or five months if you have used crystal meth. Anyone who arrives without that clean time is not admitted, so plan a stay in a detox or recovery house first if you need one.

faqs.q: Are there any age restrictions for the program?
faqs.a: Yes, the program is only available for individuals aged 19 years and above.

faqs.q: Where is Round Lake and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 200 Emery Louis Road on the Okanagan Reserve, just off Highway 97 about 22 km northwest of Vernon in BC's North Okanagan. From Vancouver it is about 5 hours by car, or you can book Ebus to Vernon and take a taxi for the last stretch. If you fly, the nearest airport is Kelowna, about an hour south. Clients and referral workers arrange and pay for travel themselves.

You leave with an aftercare and relapse prevention plan built with your counsellor, and a follow-up appointment with your home counsellor that you booked before arriving. If you stay sober, you can return for a four-week refresher program. Graduates who need more support can apply to the Painted Turtle Lodge, the 10-bed recovery home on site, for up to six months.

faqs.q: What counseling methods do they offer?
faqs.a: The program is focused on motivational experiential counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), psychodynamic therapy, and sensorimotor psychotherapies, which are conducted in a group setting.

faqs.a: Clients have access to the Recovery Lodge, which features amazing views, a gym, a library and healthy meals.
